title: Relative regular equations remain regular locally after base change
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative rings with $A$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $b\geq0$ and let $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$ be an $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and assume that $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ is flat over $R$. For any homomorphism $R\to R'$ of commutative rings, put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $f'_j=f_j\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes r)(a_1\otimes r_1)=aa_1\otimes rr_1$ and unit $1\otimes1$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ containing all the $f'_j$, the elements $f'_1/1,\ldots,f'_b/1$ form a regular sequence in the local ring $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0FUD, remark-relative-regular-immersion-elements; its algebraic base-change input is more-algebra.tex Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra.

proof.text: If $b=0$, the given prime $\mathfrak q'$ makes $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ a nonzero local ring, so the empty sequence is regular by the definition in the statement. Hence assume $b>0$. Put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$. Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] to the given regular sequence in $A$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $(A/J)[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\simeq\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$, sending $T_j$ to the degree-one class of $f_j$. This is exactly the quasi-regular hypothesis of the algebraic base-change input.

Fix the prime $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ in the statement. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be its inverse image and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image in $R$. Thus $J\subset\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=A\otimes_R k$. The fraction description of the fibre in the statement identifies $F$ with $(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(A/\mathfrak pA)$. Accordingly $\mathfrak q$ induces a prime $P$ in $F$, containing the images $\bar f_j$ of all $f_j$. Apply [lem-pur-quasi-regular-flat-quotient-base-change] to $R\to k$: the required quotient flatness is the hypothesis that $A/J$ is flat over $R$. We obtain the canonical polynomial associated-graded isomorphism for $(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_b)$ in $F$. A finite presentation of $A$ over $R$ gives a presentation of $F$ by the same generators and reduced relations over $k$; hence $F$ is finitely generated over the field $k$. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], $F$ is Noetherian. Only this fibre, not $R$ or $A$, has been asserted Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 063U, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-flat-in-neighbourhood, first proof paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 0CEP(1).

proof.text: Let $L=F_P$. It is a nonzero local Noetherian ring: for any ideal of $F_P$, generators of its contracted ideal in $F$ generate it after localization. The polynomial associated-graded isomorphism of step 2 localizes to the corresponding isomorphism for $L$ and $(\bar f_j/1)$. In detail, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies $S^{-1}(I^n/I^{n+1})$ with $(S^{-1}I)^n/(S^{-1}I)^{n+1}$ for $I=(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_b)$ and $S=F\setminus P$; powers identify by multiplying fractions. The polynomial side localizes coefficientwise, and the map still sends $T_j$ to $[\bar f_j/1]_1$. All $\bar f_j/1$ lie in the maximal ideal $PL$. Therefore [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] says they form a regular sequence in $L$.

source.place: Tag 063U proof: algebra.tex Tag 061S, lemma-quasi-regular-regular, on the Noetherian local fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to the Noetherian ring $F$, its prime $P$, and the sequence $(\bar f_j)$. It gives $\gamma\notin P$ such that the whole sequence is regular in $F[1/\gamma]$. Write $\gamma=(a\bmod\mathfrak pA)/r$ with $a\in A$ and $r\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$; then $a\notin\mathfrak q$ and $F[1/\gamma]=F[1/\bar a]$. Start with $D=A[1/a]$. This is finitely presented over $R$: to a finite presentation for $A$ adjoin one generator $u$ and relation $au-1$. It is flat over $R$: for every injection $N_1\to N_2$ of $R$-modules, flatness of $A$ first makes $N_1\otimes_RA\to N_2\otimes_RA$ injective, and exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] preserves that injection. The identifications $(N_i\otimes_RA)[1/a]\simeq N_i\otimes_RD$ send $(n\otimes x)/a^t$ to $n\otimes(x/a^t)$. Thus the fibre $D\otimes_Rk=F[1/\bar a]$ carries the regular sequence of the specified images of $f_j$.

source.place: Tag 063U proof, shrinking on the fibre by algebra.tex Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood; explicit lift of the shrinking to A.

proof.text:
We now induct on $e=0,\ldots,b$, shrinking the ambient principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ each time. The inductive claim is: there is $h
otin\mathfrak q$ and $D=A[1/h]$ such that, with $D_i=D/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$, every $D_i$ for $0\le i\le e$ is flat and finitely presented over $R$, multiplication by $f_i$ on $D_{i-1}$ is injective for $1\le i\le e$, and on the fibre $D\otimes_Rk$ all successive multiplication maps of $( ar f_1,\ldots, ar f_b)$ are injective. Step 4 gives the base case $e=0$. For the induction step apply [lem-pc-algebra-fibre-cartier-local] with base $R$, ambient algebra $D_e$, field $K=k$, principal ideal $(f_{e+1})$, and the prime $\mathfrak q_e$ induced by $\mathfrak q$. This prime exists because all $f_j\in\mathfrak q$, and its contraction is $\mathfrak p=\ker(R	o k)$. The fibre identifies with $(D\otimes_Rk)/( ar f_1,\ldots, ar f_e)$: the map sends $(d mod(f_1,\ldots,f_e))\otimes t$ to the class of $d\otimes t$, with inverse on pure tensors given by the same formula. In this fibre $ ar f_{e+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor by the inductive claim. At every fibre prime one can therefore take $g_P=1$ in the cited criterion, so its all-primes hypothesis is satisfied, not just a hypothesis at the chosen point. The criterion gives $g
otin\mathfrak q_e$ such that $(f_{e+1})$ in $(D_e)[1/g]$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor $v$ and its quotient is flat over $R$. The specified $f_{e+1}$ itself is a nonzerodivisor: writing $v=t f_{e+1}$, the equation $f_{e+1}x=0$ implies $vx=0$, hence $x=0$. Lift $g$ to $	ilde g\in D$ outside the prime induced by $\mathfrak q$, and replace $D$ by $D[1/	ilde g]$. Writing $	ilde g=c/h^n$ makes this $A[1/(hc)]$, with $hc
otin\mathfrak q$. Earlier multiplication injections and all fibre multiplication injections survive by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Earlier flat quotients remain flat by the injection-and-localization argument of step 4. Every prefix quotient remains finitely presented: append its finitely many equations to the finite presentation and append a generator and relation for each new inverse. The criterion supplies the new flat quotient $D_{e+1}$, completing the induction. Thus at $e=b$ the original equations on some $A[1/h]$, $h
otin\mathfrak q$, have all prefix quotients flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 063U proof, repeated fibre-Cartier criterion Tag 062Y; algebraic form of that criterion in the cited existing node.

proof.text: For the final $D$ of step 5, each sequence of $R$-modules $0\to D_{i-1}\xrightarrow{\ f_i\ }D_{i-1}\to D_i\to0$ is exact and its last term is flat over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with $N=R'$ to every one of them. The cited lemma first gives injection on $R'\otimes_RD_{i-1}$. The $R$-linear flip $r'\otimes d\mapsto d\otimes r'$, with inverse $d\otimes r'\mapsto r'\otimes d$, follows directly from the tensor universal property and carries $r'\otimes f_i d$ to $f_i d\otimes r'=(f_i\otimes1)(d\otimes r')$. Thus multiplication by $f_i\otimes1$ on $D_{i-1}\otimes_RR'$ is injective for every $i$. The usual tensor-quotient identification is explicit: $(d\bmod(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1}))\otimes r'$ maps to $[d\otimes r']$, and the inverse sends $[d\otimes r']$ back to this tensor. Hence the images of the $f_j$ are weakly regular on $D\otimes_RR'$. Tensoring the principal localization gives $D\otimes_RR'=A'[1/h']$, $h'=h\otimes1$, via $(a/h^n)\otimes r'\mapsto(a\otimes r')/(h')^n$ and its inverse. Since $h\notin\mathfrak q$, we have $h'\notin\mathfrak q'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] to $A'[1/h']$, its prime induced by $\mathfrak q'$, and this weakly regular sequence. All its terms lie in that prime. The resulting local ring is canonically $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$, by sending fractions to the same fractions (the extra element $h'$ is already invertible there). We obtain the required regular sequence of the specified $f'_j/1$, including the nonzero final quotient, which has residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$. This proves the arbitrary-base-change conclusion without assuming $R'$ flat over $R$.

Item statement: identical to the base and to the read-only copies in both projects. It agrees with Stacks 0FUD/063U (divisors.tex). The restriction to primes q' that contain the f'_j is needed: without it, k[t] with f=t and q'=(t-1) is a counterexample. The report records this as a source error. Steps: step 1 uses 00LN(1) (regular implies quasi-regular). Step 2 applies the new 0CEP(1) node to R→κ(p), which needs only flatness of A/J; the fibre is finite type over a field, hence Noetherian. Step 3 localizes the associated-graded isomorphism exactly and applies the new 061S node in the Noetherian local fibre. Step 4 applies the 061L node, with γ=ā/r so a∉q, then checks finite presentation and flatness of A[1/a]. Step 5 checks every hypothesis of the 062Y fibre-Cartier leaf, which is the Lean declaration Fiber.lean:981 (read): flat and finitely presented D_e, a field with kernel p, a principal ideal, and g_P=1 at all fibre primes. It also checks v=t·f_{e+1}, so f_{e+1} is a nonzerodivisor, and that each new denominator c/h^n gives a principal open not containing q. Step 6 uses 00HL with N=R' and no flatness of R', then the weakly-regular localization at q' with h'∉q'. Long step 5 (2303 characters): it is the single 063U induction, now with its invariant, base case and inductive step stated. Its only non-elementary input is the cited 062Y leaf, and the rest is short checks. Splitting it would put the whole item into a child, the D1/D2 fault this repair removed, so it may stay. New nodes: 0CEP(1) and 061S (with M=A) match their Stacks sources hypothesis by hypothesis. Both are statement-only and meet B1–B7. Small cases agree: b=0, a unit generator, Z[x]/(2x) with f=x (hypothesis fails), and k[x,y]/(xy) localized with f=x (hypothesis fails, and x is a zerodivisor). Both are strictly smaller than the item. An rg search for 0CEP, 061S, quasi-regular, 063U and 062Y found no duplicates. Mathlib RegularSequence.lean:21 lists quasi-regular sequences as TODO. Route: lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial is in unit sk-def-purity-conv, which this item's unit cites. The declared tool use lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood is in fact in the item's own unit, so the declaration is redundant; accepting it is harmless. No SGA source, no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses.
